title: 4,556 ETH lost to address poisoning (Ethereum, 30 Jan 2026)
summary: Two days after paying its OTC counterparty, the victim sent 4,556 ETH to a lookalike that had earlier sent it zero-value ETH transactions and USDC dust (as reported by Specter and Scam Sniffer).

harm.description: The victim signed a native transfer of 4,556 ETH to the lookalike (token field 0x0 = native ETH).

evaluation.rationale: The 21,600 blocks (about 3 days) before and including the harmful block: the same round default as the WBTC case, fixed before any activity in the window was examined.

onchain_verification: Verified on 2026-10-28 via eth.drpc.org: sources print the hash truncated (0x7facade9d47...); the only transaction in block 24348794 from the victim to the lookalike is 0x7facade9d4731a639c4f31e84f5dfef0ddce8d2dc4d8a4399b72cd66817a8ac7, value 4556 ETH, status success.
Verified: eth_getCode(victim) empty at block 24348794 (plain EOA); nonce 202 at block 24327194 and 220 after block 24348794.
ground_truth_limitations: Reported planting steps are zero-value ETH transactions from the lookalike to the victim (incoming native ETH, which CryptoGuard cannot see) and USDC dust about 99 days earlier (outside the window).
Attribution as poisoning rests on public analyst reports plus address similarity.
